The '''Tanabe Festival''' (田辺祭, Tanabe Matsuri) is a {{ill|festival|ja|祭り}} held in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}} for over 460 years. It serves as the {{ill|reitaisai|ja|例祭}} of {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} and is regarded as one of the "Three Great Festivals of Kishū," alongside the {{ill|Kishū Tōshō-gū|ja|和歌祭|gg=Kishū Tōshō-gū \|lt=Waka Festival}} and {{ill|Kokawa Shrine Festival|ja|粉河祭}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wakayama.keizai.biz/headline/678/|title=Kishū Three Great Festivals: Kokawa Festival held in Kinokawa City, Wakayama|newspaper=Wakayama Economic Newspaper|date=2016-08-01|accessdate=2022-05-01}}</ref>
The main events occur on July 24 (eve festival) and July 25 (main festival), with preliminary events like float testing starting in early July on a town-by-town basis.
During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40年}}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>
The festival has been designated as an {{ill|intangible folk cultural property|ja|無形民俗文化財}} of Wakayama Prefecture.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties in Tanabe City - Intangible Folk Cultural Properties|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_minzokubunkazai.html|website=Tanabe City|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties - Folk Cultural Properties|url=https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/d00155461.html|website=Wakayama Prefectural Board of Education|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref>
== Overview ==
The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

The '''Tanabe Festival''' (田辺祭, Tanabe Matsuri) is a {{ill|festival|ja|祭り}} held in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}} for over 460 years. It serves as the {{ill|reitaisai|ja|例祭}} of {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} and is regarded as one of the "Three Great Festivals of Kishū," alongside the {{ill|Kishū Tōshō-gū|ja|和歌祭|gg=Kishū Tōshō-gū \|lt=Waka Festival}} and {{ill|Kokawa Shrine Festival|ja|粉河祭}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wakayama.keizai.biz/headline/678/|title=Kishū Three Great Festivals: Kokawa Festival held in Kinokawa City, Wakayama|newspaper=Wakayama Economic Newspaper|date=2016-08-01|accessdate=2022-05-01}}</ref>
The main events occur on July 24 (eve festival) and July 25 (main festival), with preliminary events like float testing starting in early July on a town-by-town basis.
During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40年}}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>
The festival has been designated as an {{ill|intangible folk cultural property|ja|無形民俗文化財}} of Wakayama Prefecture.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties in Tanabe City - Intangible Folk Cultural Properties|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_minzokubunkazai.html|website=Tanabe City|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties - Folk Cultural Properties|url=https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/d00155461.html|website=Wakayama Prefectural Board of Education|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref>
== Overview ==
The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

The '''Tanabe Festival''' (田辺祭, Tanabe Matsuri) is a {{ill|festival|ja|祭り}} held in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}} for over 460 years. It serves as the {{ill|reitaisai|ja|例祭}} of {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} and is regarded as one of the "Three Great Festivals of Kishū," alongside the {{ill|Kishū Tōshō-gū|ja|和歌祭|gg=Kishū Tōshō-gū \|lt=Waka Festival}} and {{ill|Kokawa Shrine Festival|ja|粉河祭}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wakayama.keizai.biz/headline/678/|title=Kishū Three Great Festivals: Kokawa Festival held in Kinokawa City, Wakayama|newspaper=Wakayama Economic Newspaper|date=2016-08-01|accessdate=2022-05-01}}</ref>
The main events occur on July 24 (eve festival) and July 25 (main festival), with preliminary events like float testing starting in early July on a town-by-town basis.
During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40年}}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>
The festival has been designated as an {{ill|intangible folk cultural property|ja|無形民俗文化財}} of Wakayama Prefecture.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties in Tanabe City - Intangible Folk Cultural Properties|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_minzokubunkazai.html|website=Tanabe City|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties - Folk Cultural Properties|url=https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/d00155461.html|website=Wakayama Prefectural Board of Education|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref>
== Overview ==
The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

The '''Tanabe Festival''' (田辺祭, Tanabe Matsuri) is a {{ill|festival|ja|祭り}} held in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}} for over 460 years. It serves as the {{ill|reitaisai|ja|例祭}} of {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} and is regarded as one of the "Three Great Festivals of Kishū," alongside the {{ill|Kishū Tōshō-gū|ja|和歌祭|gg=Kishū Tōshō-gū \|lt=Waka Festival}} and {{ill|Kokawa Shrine Festival|ja|粉河祭}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wakayama.keizai.biz/headline/678/|title=Kishū Three Great Festivals: Kokawa Festival held in Kinokawa City, Wakayama|newspaper=Wakayama Economic Newspaper|date=2016-08-01|accessdate=2022-05-01}}</ref>
The main events occur on July 24 (eve festival) and July 25 (main festival), with preliminary events like float testing starting in early July on a town-by-town basis.
During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40年}}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>
The festival has been designated as an {{ill|intangible folk cultural property|ja|無形民俗文化財}} of Wakayama Prefecture.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties in Tanabe City - Intangible Folk Cultural Properties|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_minzokubunkazai.html|website=Tanabe City|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties - Folk Cultural Properties|url=https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/d00155461.html|website=Wakayama Prefectural Board of Education|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref>
== Overview ==
The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

The '''Tanabe Festival''' (田辺祭, Tanabe Matsuri) is a {{ill|festival|ja|祭り}} held in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}} for over 460 years. It serves as the {{ill|reitaisai|ja|例祭}} of {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} and is regarded as one of the "Three Great Festivals of Kishū," alongside the {{ill|Kishū Tōshō-gū|ja|和歌祭|gg=Kishū Tōshō-gū \|lt=Waka Festival}} and {{ill|Kokawa Shrine Festival|ja|粉河祭}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wakayama.keizai.biz/headline/678/|title=Kishū Three Great Festivals: Kokawa Festival held in Kinokawa City, Wakayama|newspaper=Wakayama Economic Newspaper|date=2016-08-01|accessdate=2022-05-01}}</ref>
The main events occur on July 24 (eve festival) and July 25 (main festival), with preliminary events like float testing starting in early July on a town-by-town basis.
During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40年}}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>
The festival has been designated as an {{ill|intangible folk cultural property|ja|無形民俗文化財}} of Wakayama Prefecture.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties in Tanabe City - Intangible Folk Cultural Properties|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_minzokubunkazai.html|website=Tanabe City|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties - Folk Cultural Properties|url=https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/d00155461.html|website=Wakayama Prefectural Board of Education|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref>
== Overview ==
The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>

== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>

During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40年}}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>
The festival has been designated as an {{ill|intangible folk cultural property|ja|無形民俗文化財}} of Wakayama Prefecture.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties in Tanabe City - Intangible Folk Cultural Properties|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_minzokubunkazai.html|website=Tanabe City|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties - Folk Cultural Properties|url=https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/d00155461.html|website=Wakayama Prefectural Board of Education|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref>
== Overview ==
The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

The '''Tanabe Festival''' (田辺祭, Tanabe Matsuri) is a {{ill|festival|ja|祭り}} held in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}} for over 460 years. It serves as the {{ill|reitaisai|ja|例祭}} of {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} and is regarded as one of the "Three Great Festivals of Kishū," alongside the {{ill|Kishū Tōshō-gū|ja|和歌祭|gg=Kishū Tōshō-gū \|lt=Waka Festival}} and {{ill|Kokawa Shrine Festival|ja|粉河祭}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wakayama.keizai.biz/headline/678/|title=Kishū Three Great Festivals: Kokawa Festival held in Kinokawa City, Wakayama|newspaper=Wakayama Economic Newspaper|date=2016-08-01|accessdate=2022-05-01}}</ref>
The main events occur on July 24 (eve festival) and July 25 (main festival), with preliminary events like float testing starting in early July on a town-by-town basis.
During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40年}}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>
The festival has been designated as an {{ill|intangible folk cultural property|ja|無形民俗文化財}} of Wakayama Prefecture.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties in Tanabe City - Intangible Folk Cultural Properties|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_minzokubunkazai.html|website=Tanabe City|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties - Folk Cultural Properties|url=https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/d00155461.html|website=Wakayama Prefectural Board of Education|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref>
== Overview ==
The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

The '''Tanabe Festival''' (田辺祭, Tanabe Matsuri) is a {{ill|festival|ja|祭り}} held in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}} for over 460 years. It serves as the {{ill|reitaisai|ja|例祭}} of {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} and is regarded as one of the "Three Great Festivals of Kishū," alongside the {{ill|Kishū Tōshō-gū|ja|和歌祭|gg=Kishū Tōshō-gū \|lt=Waka Festival}} and {{ill|Kokawa Shrine Festival|ja|粉河祭}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wakayama.keizai.biz/headline/678/|title=Kishū Three Great Festivals: Kokawa Festival held in Kinokawa City, Wakayama|newspaper=Wakayama Economic Newspaper|date=2016-08-01|accessdate=2022-05-01}}</ref>
The main events occur on July 24 (eve festival) and July 25 (main festival), with preliminary events like float testing starting in early July on a town-by-town basis.
During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40年}}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>
The festival has been designated as an {{ill|intangible folk cultural property|ja|無形民俗文化財}} of Wakayama Prefecture.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties in Tanabe City - Intangible Folk Cultural Properties|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_minzokubunkazai.html|website=Tanabe City|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties - Folk Cultural Properties|url=https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/d00155461.html|website=Wakayama Prefectural Board of Education|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref>
== Overview ==
The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

It serves as the {{ill|reitaisai|ja|例祭}} of {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} and is regarded as one of the "Three Great Festivals of Kishū," alongside the {{ill|Kishū Tōshō-gū|ja|和歌祭|gg=Kishū Tōshō-gū \|lt=Waka Festival}} and {{ill|Kokawa Shrine Festival|ja|粉河祭}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wakayama.keizai.biz/headline/678/|title=Kishū Three Great Festivals: Kokawa Festival held in Kinokawa City, Wakayama|newspaper=Wakayama Economic Newspaper|date=2016-08-01|accessdate=2022-05-01}}</ref>
The main events occur on July 24 (eve festival) and July 25 (main festival), with preliminary events like float testing starting in early July on a town-by-town basis.
During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40年}}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>

It serves as the {{ill|reitaisai|ja|例祭}} of {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} and is regarded as one of the "Three Great Festivals of Kishū," alongside the {{ill|Kishū Tōshō-gū|ja|和歌祭|gg=Kishū Tōshō-gū \|lt=Waka Festival}} and {{ill|Kokawa Shrine Festival|ja|粉河祭}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wakayama.keizai.biz/headline/678/|title=Kishū Three Great Festivals: Kokawa Festival held in Kinokawa City, Wakayama|newspaper=Wakayama Economic Newspaper|date=2016-08-01|accessdate=2022-05-01}}</ref>
The main events occur on July 24 (eve festival) and July 25 (main festival), with preliminary events like float testing starting in early July on a town-by-town basis.
During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40年}}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>
The festival has been designated as an {{ill|intangible folk cultural property|ja|無形民俗文化財}} of Wakayama Prefecture.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties in Tanabe City - Intangible Folk Cultural Properties|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_minzokubunkazai.html|website=Tanabe City|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties - Folk Cultural Properties|url=https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/d00155461.html|website=Wakayama Prefectural Board of Education|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref>
== Overview ==
The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

The '''Tanabe Festival''' (田辺祭, Tanabe Matsuri) is a {{ill|festival|ja|祭り}} held in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}} for over 460 years. It serves as the {{ill|reitaisai|ja|例祭}} of {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} and is regarded as one of the "Three Great Festivals of Kishū," alongside the {{ill|Kishū Tōshō-gū|ja|和歌祭|gg=Kishū Tōshō-gū \|lt=Waka Festival}} and {{ill|Kokawa Shrine Festival|ja|粉河祭}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wakayama.keizai.biz/headline/678/|title=Kishū Three Great Festivals: Kokawa Festival held in Kinokawa City, Wakayama|newspaper=Wakayama Economic Newspaper|date=2016-08-01|accessdate=2022-05-01}}</ref>
The main events occur on July 24 (eve festival) and July 25 (main festival), with preliminary events like float testing starting in early July on a town-by-town basis.
During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40年}}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>
The festival has been designated as an {{ill|intangible folk cultural property|ja|無形民俗文化財}} of Wakayama Prefecture.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties in Tanabe City - Intangible Folk Cultural Properties|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_minzokubunkazai.html|website=Tanabe City|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties - Folk Cultural Properties|url=https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/d00155461.html|website=Wakayama Prefectural Board of Education|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref>
== Overview ==
The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. The '''Tanabe Festival''' (田辺祭, Tanabe Matsuri) is a {{ill|festival|ja|祭り}} held in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}} for over 460 years. It serves as the {{ill|reitaisai|ja|例祭}} of {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} and is regarded as one of the "Three Great Festivals of Kishū," alongside the {{ill|Kishū Tōshō-gū|ja|和歌祭|gg=Kishū Tōshō-gū \|lt=Waka Festival}} and {{ill|Kokawa Shrine Festival|ja|粉河祭}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wakayama.keizai.biz/headline/678/|title=Kishū Three Great Festivals: Kokawa Festival held in Kinokawa City, Wakayama|newspaper=Wakayama Economic Newspaper|date=2016-08-01|accessdate=2022-05-01}}</ref>
The main events occur on July 24 (eve festival) and July 25 (main festival), with preliminary events like float testing starting in early July on a town-by-town basis.
During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40年}}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>

The '''Tanabe Festival''' (田辺祭, Tanabe Matsuri) is a {{ill|festival|ja|祭り}} held in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}} for over 460 years. It serves as the {{ill|reitaisai|ja|例祭}} of {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} and is regarded as one of the "Three Great Festivals of Kishū," alongside the {{ill|Kishū Tōshō-gū|ja|和歌祭|gg=Kishū Tōshō-gū \|lt=Waka Festival}} and {{ill|Kokawa Shrine Festival|ja|粉河祭}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wakayama.keizai.biz/headline/678/|title=Kishū Three Great Festivals: Kokawa Festival held in Kinokawa City, Wakayama|newspaper=Wakayama Economic Newspaper|date=2016-08-01|accessdate=2022-05-01}}</ref>
The main events occur on July 24 (eve festival) and July 25 (main festival), with preliminary events like float testing starting in early July on a town-by-town basis.
During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40th year }}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>
The festival has been designated as an {{ill|intangible folk cultural property|ja|無形民俗文化財}} of Wakayama Prefecture.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties in Tanabe City - Intangible Folk Cultural Properties|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_minzokubunkazai.html|website=Tanabe City|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties - Folk Cultural Properties|url=https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/d00155461.html|website=Wakayama Prefectural Board of Education|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref>
== Overview ==
The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

{{Multiple issues | Refimprove = July 2019 | Vague = May 2022 | Original research = May 2022 }} {{Event information | Event name = Tanabe Festival | English name = | image = Tanabe Festival (Tōkei Shrine).jpg | image size = 300px | image description = Parade at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}} approach (2018) | Type = {{ill|Festival|ja|祭り|12=draft}} | Nickname = | Formal name = Tōkei Shrine Reitaisai | Old name = | Held = Annually July 24 (eve) and July 25 (main festival) | First held = Mid-16th century | Last held = | Time = | Venue = | Organizer = | Co-organizer = | Sponsors = | Planning = | Cooperation = | Management = | Producer = | Exhibitors = | Visitors = | Access = | Nearest station = Kii-Tanabe Station, Wakayama Prefecture | Direct bus = | Parking = | URL = http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ | Notes = }}
The '''Tanabe Festival''' (田辺祭, Tanabe Matsuri) is a {{ill|festival|ja|祭り|12=draft}} held in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県|12=draft}} for over 460 years. It serves as the {{ill|reitaisai|ja|例祭|12=draft}} of {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}} and is regarded as one of the "Three Great Festivals of Kishū," alongside the {{ill|Kishū Tōshō-gū|ja|和歌祭|gg=Kishū Tōshō-gū \|lt=Waka Festival|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kokawa Shrine Festival|ja|粉河祭|12=draft}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wakayama.keizai.biz/headline/678/|title=Kishū Three Great Festivals: Kokawa Festival held in Kinokawa City, Wakayama|newspaper=Wakayama Economic Newspaper|date=2016-08-01|accessdate=2022-05-01}}</ref>
The main events occur on July 24 (eve festival) and July 25 (main festival), with preliminary events like float testing starting in early July on a town-by-town basis.
During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40th year|12=draft}}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>
The festival has been designated as an {{ill|intangible folk cultural property|ja|無形民俗文化財|12=draft}} of Wakayama Prefecture.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties in Tanabe City - Intangible Folk Cultural Properties|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_minzokubunkazai.html|website=Tanabe City|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties - Folk Cultural Properties|url=https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/d00155461.html|website=Wakayama Prefectural Board of Education|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref>
== Overview ==
The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿|12=draft}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬|12=draft}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城|12=draft}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)|12=draft}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿|12=draft}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬|12=draft}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城|12=draft}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)|12=draft}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>

{{Multiple issues | Refimprove = July 2019 | Vague = May 2022 | Original research = May 2022 }} {{Event information | Event name = Tanabe Festival | English name = | image = Tanabe Festival (Tōkei Shrine).jpg | image size = 300px | image description = Parade at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}} approach (2018) | Type = {{ill|Festival|ja|祭り|12=draft}} | Nickname = | Formal name = Tōkei Shrine Reitaisai | Old name = | Held = Annually July 24 (eve) and July 25 (main festival) | First held = Mid-16th century | Last held = | Time = | Venue = | Organizer = | Co-organizer = | Sponsors = | Planning = | Cooperation = | Management = | Producer = | Exhibitors = | Visitors = | Access = | Nearest station = Kii-Tanabe Station, Wakayama Prefecture | Direct bus = | Parking = | URL = http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ | Notes = }}
The '''Tanabe Festival''' (田辺祭, Tanabe Matsuri) is a {{ill|festival|ja|祭り|12=draft}} held in {{ill|Tanabe|ja|田辺市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県|12=draft}} for over 460 years. It serves as the {{ill|reitaisai|ja|例祭|12=draft}} of {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}} and is regarded as one of the "Three Great Festivals of Kishū," alongside the {{ill|Kishū Tōshō-gū|ja|和歌祭|gg=Kishū Tōshō-gū \|lt=Waka Festival|12=draft}} and {{ill|Kokawa Shrine Festival|ja|粉河祭|12=draft}}.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://wakayama.keizai.biz/headline/678/|title=Kishū Three Great Festivals: Kokawa Festival held in Kinokawa City, Wakayama|newspaper=Wakayama Economic Newspaper|date=2016-08-01|accessdate=2022-05-01}}</ref>
The main events occur on July 24 (eve festival) and July 25 (main festival), with preliminary events like float testing starting in early July on a town-by-town basis.
During the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, the festival was held on June 24 and June 25 but was shifted to the current dates in {{ill|1907|ja|明治40th year|12=draft}}.<ref name="Hirano">{{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|pp=108-109}}</ref>
The festival has been designated as an {{ill|intangible folk cultural property|ja|無形民俗文化財|12=draft}} of Wakayama Prefecture.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=List of Designated Cultural Properties in Tanabe City - Intangible Folk Cultural Properties|url=http://www.city.tanabe.lg.jp/bunshin/bunkazai/shiteibunkazai_minzokubunkazai.html|website=Tanabe City|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|title=Prefectural Designated Cultural Properties - Folk Cultural Properties|url=https://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/d00155461.html|website=Wakayama Prefectural Board of Education|accessdate=2019-07-13}}</ref>
== Overview ==
The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿|12=draft}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬|12=draft}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城|12=draft}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)|12=draft}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|12=draft}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>
== References == === Notes === {{notelist}} === Citations === <references />
== Bibliography == {{Cite book|和書|author=Hirano Koji|title=Tanabe Festival: Hirano Koji Photo Collection|publisher=Kii Minpo Publishing|year=2012|isbn=978-4907841102|ref=harv}}

== Overview ==
The festival features a procession with {{ill|mikoshi|ja|神輿|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, floats (''kasahoko''), and equestrian events such as {{ill|yabusame|ja|流鏑馬|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The parade proceeds from {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} through former {{ill|Tanabe Castle|ja|田辺城|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'s castle town.<ref name="tanbo2">[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/kasahoko/ Kasahoko Parade - Tanabe City Tourism Association]</ref>
While the float parade is widely known, the festival is divided into three main components: - Mikoshi procession and ''akatsuki no saiten'' (dawn ritual) led by {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. - Equestrian displays organized by five towns. - Float procession hosted by preservation groups in eight towns.
Four additional shrines outside Tōkei Shrine's parish (Yatate Inari Shrine, {{ill|Aritōshi Shrine (Tanabe)|ja|蟻通神社 (田辺市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Kagura Shrine, and Hiyoshi Shrine) also participate in the festival.<ref>[https://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/460.pdf/ Kasahoko Parade Routes - Tanabe Tourism Association]</ref>
=== Annual Schedule ===
The festival's main schedule is outlined by the Tanabe Tourism Association.<ref>[http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/ About Tanabe Festival] - Tanabe Tourism Association</ref>
==== Eve Festival (July 24) ==== * 8:30 AM: Floats gather at the designated locations. * 8:45 AM: Mikoshi procession departs {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * 9:15 AM: Mikoshi crosses Aizu Bridge and reaches the ''otabisho'' (temporary shrine). * 10:50 AM: Sacred dances, including ''Suzumai'' and ''Urayasu no Mai,'' are performed. * 1:20 PM: Mikoshi returns to {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Floats parade through town, visiting ''oyado'' (temporary lodging shrines). * 7:00 PM: Final parade at the shrine approach. * 9:30 PM: Floats disperse to their respective lodgings.
==== Main Festival (July 25) ==== * 4:30 AM: ''Akatsuki no Saiten'' (dawn ritual) with dances performed at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * 12:00 PM: Floats gather again for the main procession. * 7:30 PM: Floats perform ''omiyairi'' (formal entry) at {{ill|Tōkei Shrine|ja|鬪雞神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * 9:20 PM: Equestrian displays conclude the festival.
== Mikoshi == The mikoshi procession includes shrine officials, miko (shrine maidens), guards, and accompanying participants.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Yabusame == Yabusame refers to archery performed on horseback and also designates the equestrian towns responsible for specific roles.<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.tanabe-kanko.jp/event/tanabematsuri/midokoro/|title=Yabusame|publisher=Tanabe Tourism Association|work=Festival Highlights|accessdate=2020-05-02}}</ref>
== Floats == Floats (''kasahoko'') are a key feature of the festival. Each float is adorned with unique decorations and performances by children and adults.<ref name="tanbo2" />
== Tradition and Continuity == The Tanabe Festival has faced challenges due to urban depopulation and aging demographics. Efforts are ongoing to ensure its continuation, including participation from younger generations and cultural preservation.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.agara.co.jp/article/310711|title=How to Sustain the Tanabe Festival|newspaper=Kii Minpo|date=2023-10-06|accessdate=2023-10-08}}</ref>
